mappings.note: Names two nitrogen-fixing bacteria. Organism-level recall, C4.3 - the same code as O52, since a very-short and an MCQ version of one fact cannot be split by any outcome in this frame.
Defines nitrification, naming Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter and the ammonia-nitrite-nitrate conversion. Microbial interaction inside the cycle, C4.3. No chart is produced, so LO-56 stays out.

Defines denitrification as bacteria returning soil nitrate to atmospheric N2. C4.3, and deliberately the same code as V81 - the two are complementary halves of one microbial story, and S114 later asks for exactly that comparison.

Where oxygen sits in combined form: metal oxides in the crust and CO2 in the air. Those are geosphere and atmosphere reservoirs, named only in the competency. C4.3 is withheld because no organism appears in the answer.

What a eutrophic water body looks like - algal blooms, oxygen depletion, fish kill. Observation at the ecosystem level, C4.3. Unlike its siblings it does not ask for the agricultural cause, so C2.8 is not needed.

Ground-level smog from vehicular emissions reacting in sunlight. POOR FIT: air pollution chemistry has no outcome in this frame, and the sunlight here is a reagent rather than a band being discriminated, so LO-3 would overstate it.

Deforestation changing surface albedo AND transpiration - both sit in LO-5 (surface interaction, and 'evaporation'). C2.8 carries the human land-use cause. This is the albedo item whose driver is a human change rather than a material.

POOR FIT and a finding. The outcome of the Montreal Protocol - a treaty's success. Policy and international cooperation have no outcome anywhere in this frame; C5.3/CG5 is the only legal code reaching outside science.

78 per cent nitrogen, 21 per cent oxygen. POOR FIT: atmospheric composition is recall with no mechanism, and no outcome in the frame mentions the atmosphere's makeup. Grouped with O23, O10 and O57 as the composition/structure gap.

Cryosphere to hydrosphere to biosphere, three spheres named in the stem. LO-55 is the only code that names them. Distinguished from N13 only by starting in the cryosphere rather than the atmosphere; the outcome is honestly shared.

Two demands: which bands dominate the arriving radiation (LO-2, the beam's composition) and how the atmosphere treats UV versus IR differently (LO-3, band-selective behaviour). Both clauses are genuinely exercised, so both are cited.
Defines insolation and the solar constant and explains the gap between them. Entirely about the incoming beam and its attenuation - LO-2. Nothing here distinguishes bands, so LO-3 is not engaged.

Part two asks why the stratosphere warms with height - ozone absorbing UV, LO-3. Part one asks where weather forms, and the answer is surface heating driving rising air, LO-5. The layer names themselves have no outcome.

Remove the atmosphere and the surface's re-radiated heat escapes - LO-5's interaction clause argued counterfactually. Same outcome as V69 but at three marks with an explicit greenhouse-mechanism demand; the frame offers no finer code.

Compares the albedo of snow and black soil and what each absorbs. LO-5's surface clause, the single outcome the whole albedo family shares. No latitude, tilt or breeze element, so no second code is warranted.

Refutes a stated misconception (that concrete reflects most radiation). The science is identical to S94's - LO-5's surface clause - and the frame has no outcome expressing the evaluate-a-claim demand that actually separates them.

Spherical shape AND axial tilt producing uneven heating - two of LO-4's three named causes in one stem. The cleanest LO-4 item in the chapter, and nothing here touches surface properties or atmospheric phenomena.

Explains eutrophication end to end, finishing at oxygen depletion killing aquatic life - C4.3's ecosystem interactions. C2.8 carries the fertiliser-overuse cause. The three-mark prose version of O9/O19/O44.

The equatorial low forms from intense heating at the equator (latitude, LO-4) and the sub-tropical high from that risen air sinking (air movement, LO-5). Both outcomes are needed because the item traces the cause into the phenomenon.

Two named roles: ozone shielding against UV (band-selective, LO-3) and greenhouse gases trapping the infrared the surface re-radiates (LO-5). The item is explicitly scored on both, so both codes are cited rather than one.

'DRAW a neat diagram illustrating the mountain breeze' - LO-56 names drawing for 'differential heating of the Earth's surface', which is exactly what a breeze diagram represents. LO-5 supplies the breeze content and the agricultural half.

Ocean currents driven by temperature and salinity differences at depth. POOR FIT: thermohaline circulation is a hydrosphere process with no outcome; LO-5's atmospheric phenomena do not reach it, so only the competency is honest here.

'DRAW a schematic diagram of the carbon cycle' - LO-56's verb applied to its named subject, biogeochemical cycles. C4.3 carries the fast-cycle biology. This drawing demand is what separates it from S105 and L119.

Climate change perturbing the water cycle, with coastal and agricultural consequences in India. C2.8 carries the cross-sphere disruption; LO-5 contributes only through 'evaporation', the frame's single water-cycle word.

Traces a nitrogen atom from air to plant to animal and back - a path told in prose, so C4.3 rather than LO-56. The atom passing between trophic levels is exactly C4.3's 'organisms to ecosystems' interaction.
